_status: DRAFT — proposed, not approved. Merge into requirements.json only after review.

requirements.title: Staff roles are held by parties for a period and recorded at decision time
requirements.rationale: Approving authority belongs to an office — Forest Committee Chair, President — not permanently to a person. Roles are assignable and revocable, and every approval records the role held at the moment of decision so a later change of office never rewrites the history of a decision.

requirements.title: Approval policies are data, not code
requirements.rationale: permissions.json already names dual_control and ai_release_review but never defines them. Defining them as records means the control can be tightened — raising minimum_approvals when a third authorized person exists — without a code change, consistent with how the rest of the platform treats the specification as the source of truth.

requirements.title: A requester may never approve their own request
requirements.rationale: Separation of duties is the entire point of dual control. Enforced by a database constraint as well as in code, because a control that lives only in application logic is one refactor away from being lost.

requirements.title: Approvals bind to the exact resource version being approved
requirements.rationale: Approving a parcel rather than a specific boundary version would let a submitter replace the boundary after approval and inherit it. Approvals therefore reference the immutable version identifier.

requirements.title: Approval decisions are append-only and auditable
requirements.rationale: A decision is never updated or deleted. Reconsideration supersedes the request and raises a new one, so an audit can always answer who approved what, when, and in what capacity. Supports TEST-018 release certification.
